newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel French group rejects debt plan.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel French group rejects debt plan.

text.p: A French small shareholders group, Adacte, recommended on Monday that stockholders of Eurotunnel SA/Plc reject a 70 billion franc debt restructuring plan when it is put to a vote on July 10.
The Association de Defense des Actionnaires d'Eurotunnel said that in view of 15 major risks, it recommended a "massive and clear no" at the shareholders meeting.
Adacte, whose members include mostly retired people, mustered proxies representing about four percent of votes at the 1996 annual shareholders meeting.

"Even after the financial restructuring, Eurotunnel will have significantly and permanently to improve its operational performance in order to satisfy its commitments on debt and interest payments," Adacte said in a statement.
It also attacked the creditor banks' right to take control of the Channel Tunnel under a "substitution" clause.

French lawyer Sophie L'Helias said in an interview in Investir weekly on Saturday that she represented institutional shareholders who would approve the debt restructuring on condition Eurotunnel's bankers abandon 25 percent of their loans. They are also calling for the banks to drop their legal right to take over the Tunnel through substitution.
Eurotunnel needs unanimous approval by its bank lenders and two-thirds of the French and 75 percent of British shareholders.
Eurotunnel executive chairman Patrick Ponsolle has said the company would likely seek creditor protection if the restructuring were not approved.
Under the terms of the debt deal, banks would swap eight billion francs of loans for Eurotunnel shares, dluting current equity holders to 54.5 percent of the capital.
